input.rationale: With only 3 merit measurements, I sampled along the Fe axis. The photocurrent went up steadily with Fe content: 8 (V-rich) gave 2e-8 A, 160 (Fe:V near 1:1, FeVO4-like) gave 1.2e-7 A, and 145 (the most Fe-rich candidate in the library, lowest V) gave 4.8e-7 A. This fits Fe-oxide-rich absorbers being the most active under 2.72 eV light.

content.text:
I submitted index 145 (Fe 0.62, Ni 0.22, V 0.16) as the best composition, with a photocurrent of 4.8e-7 A. That's the best of the three I could measure. Whether it's the best in the 200-candidate library is unknown.

I spent all 3 merit measurements on points spread along the Fe axis:

| Index | Composition (Fe / Ni / V) | Photocurrent (A) |
|---|---|---|
| 8 | 0.17 / 0.17 / 0.66 (V-rich) | 2e-8 |
| 160 | 0.41 / 0.18 / 0.41 (FeVO₄-like, Fe:V ≈ 1:1) | 1.2e-7 |
| 145 | 0.62 / 0.22 / 0.16 (most Fe-rich candidate) | 4.8e-7 |

Photocurrent rose steadily with Fe content, about 4× per step. That suggests the Fe-rich corner is the most active under 2.72 eV light. Three points is still a thin basis: I tested nothing in the Ni-rich region, and none of the other Fe-rich candidates next to 145.

I didn't use any of the 5 XRD measurements or read the phase list, so which crystal phases are present is unconfirmed.
